result.topic_en: Worked examples (divisors 23, 41, 73, 77) of Euler's residue algorithm for finding the least exponent x such that 2^x ∓ 1 is divisible by a given number N.

Corollarium.

§. 9. Quoniam has operationes clare descripsimus,
eas adplicemus ad casus magis speciales. Ac primo quidem
occurrit formula $2^x \mp 1$. Pro variis igitur diuisoribus
quaeramus exponentem $x$, vt potestas $2^x$ residuum relin-
quat $\mp 1$. Sufficiet autem hoc residuum $+1$ statuisse;
si enim $2^x$ fuerit minima potestas residuum dans $= +1$;
tum potestas $2^{\frac{1}{2}x}$ necessario dabit residuum $= -1$, siqui-
dem $x$ fuerit numerus par; sin autem $x$ fuerit impar, hic
casus plane est impossibilis.

Exemplum 1.

§. 10. Quaeratur minima potestas $2^x$, quae per
23 diuisa relinquat 1, siue vt $2^x - 1$ diuisibilis fiat per
23. Hic igitur est $N = 23$; $a = 2$ et primum residuum
$= 1$; vnde operationes nostrae sequenti modo procedent:
$1 + 23 = 24 = 2^3 . 3$
$3 - 23 = -20 = -2^2 . 5$
$-5 - 23 = -28 = -2^2 . 7$
$-7 + 23 = +16 = +2^4 . 1.$
Sic iam peruentum est ad residuum optatum $+1$, ob
$f = 1$; sicque concludimus $x = 11$. Cum ergo formula
$2^{11} - 1$ sit diuisibilis per 23 et 11 numerus impar, nulla
plane datur formula $2^x + 1$ per 23 diuisibilis.
Exem-

Exemplum 2.

§. 11. Proponatur diuisor 41, per quem formula
$2^x - 1$ reddi debeat diuisibilis. Ergo ob $N = 41$; $a = 2$;
$f = 1$ et primum residuum $= 1$, habebimus:
$1 - 41 = -40 = -2^3 . 5$
$-5 + 41 = +36 = +2^2 . 9$
$+9 - 41 = -32 = -2^5 . 1.$
Hic iam subsistere possumus; cum enim potestas $2^{x-10}$ re-
linquat $-1$, eius quadratum $2^{2x-20}$ relinquet $+1$, et per
primam formam diuidendo prodit $2^{x-20}$ pro residuo $+1$
optato; sicque habemus $x = 20$. Simul autem hinc patet,
potestati $2^{10}$ residuum conuenire $-1$. ita vt formulae sim-
plicissimae per 41 diuisibiles sint: $2^{10} + 1$ et $2^{20} - 1$.

Exemplum 3.

§. 12. Pro diuisore 73 quaeratur formula simpli-
cissima $2^x \mp 1$ per eum diuisibilis. Hic est $N = 73$;
$a = 2$; et sumto primo residuo $= +1$ fiet
$1 - 73 = -72 = -2^3 . 9$
$-9 + 73 = +64 = +2^6 . 1$
vbi ergo iam subsistere licet, eritque $x = 9$, vnde formu-
la $2^9 - 1$ per 73 est diuisibilis; et quia 9 est numerus im-
par, nulla plane datur formula $2^x + 1$ per eundem nu-
merum N diuisibilis.

Exemplum 4.

§. 13. Proponatur diuisor $N = 77$ et sumto pri-
mo residuo $= 1$, calculus ita se habebit:

items.quote:
si enim $2^x$ fuerit minima potestas residuum dans $= +1$;
tum potestas $2^{\frac{1}{2}x}$ necessario dabit residuum $= -1$, siqui-
dem $x$ fuerit numerus par; sin autem $x$ fuerit impar, hic
casus plane est impossibilis.
items.english: For if $2^x$ is the least power giving residue $+1$, then the power $2^{x/2}$ will necessarily give residue $-1$, provided $x$ is even; but if $x$ is odd, this case is altogether impossible.

items.quote:
Quaeratur minima potestas $2^x$, quae per
23 diuisa relinquat 1, siue vt $2^x - 1$ diuisibilis fiat per
23.
items.english: Find the least power $2^x$ which leaves remainder 1 when divided by 23, i.e. such that $2^x - 1$ is divisible by 23.

items.quote:
Proponatur diuisor 41, per quem formula
$2^x - 1$ reddi debeat diuisibilis.
items.english: Let the divisor 41 be proposed, by which the formula $2^x - 1$ is to be made divisible.

items.quote:
Pro diuisore 73 quaeratur formula simpli-
cissima $2^x \mp 1$ per eum diuisibilis.
items.english: For the divisor 73, find the simplest formula $2^x \mp 1$ divisible by it.
